event.title: FIFA President Infantino Defends World Cup Amid Criticism
event.canonical_title: FIFA President Infantino Defends World Cup Amid Criticism
event.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has responded to critics of the World Cup, accusing them of being 'consumed by hate' and spreading false narratives. In a strongly worded statement, he suggested that detractors should 'meditate, pray or watch a football match' instead of perpetuating negativity. Infantino defended the tournament as a celebration of unity, safety, and inclusion, dismissing concerns about corruption and disciplinary rulings.

timeline.title: FIFA's $20 Billion World Cup Plan Faces Backlash from UEFA
timeline.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced a plan to establish a $20 billion US company to manage the World Cup, backed by private investors including the Kushner family. The proposal has drawn immediate criticism from UEFA, the governing body for European soccer, expressing strong opposition to the initiative.
key_facts: FIFA plans to create a $20 billion US company to run the World Cup.
The plan involves private investors, including the Kushner family.
UEFA has expressed strong opposition to the proposal.

timeline.title: FIFA Faces Backlash Over Proposal to Sell World Cup Stakes
timeline.summary: FIFA's recent proposal to sell a stake in the World Cup has sparked significant backlash from football governing bodies. Critics argue that under Gianni Infantino's leadership, FIFA has become overly focused on profit. However, FIFA has clarified that the proposal is not an obligation, but rather a suggestion.
key_facts: FIFA proposed selling a stake in the World Cup.
The proposal has been met with strong criticism from the football community.
FIFA stated that the proposal is not an obligation.

timeline.title: UEFA Threatens Boycott of World Cups Over FIFA's Investor Plan
timeline.summary: UEFA has declared its intent to boycott future FIFA World Cups if FIFA President Gianni Infantino's proposal to allow private investors to control the tournament's commercial rights is implemented. During an emergency meeting, all 55 member associations of UEFA voted unanimously in favor of this stance, emphasizing that 'the World Cup is not for sale.'
key_facts: UEFA opposes FIFA's plan for private investment in World Cup rights.
All 55 UEFA member associations voted to boycott future tournaments if the plan is adopted.
'The World Cup is not for sale,' UEFA stated.

timeline.title: FIFA President Infantino Faces Pressure After Senior Advisor Resigns Over Investment Plans
timeline.summary: Carlos Cordeiro, a senior advisor to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, has resigned amid growing backlash against Infantino's proposal for private investment in the World Cup. The resignation follows condemnation from regional football federations, including North America and Europe, which have rejected the investment plan. Critics argue that selling stakes in the World Cup could harm the integrity of football.

The resignation is linked to Infantino's proposal for private investment in the World Cup.
Regional football federations have condemned the investment plan.

event_overview.title: About the 2026 FIFA World Cup
event_overview.subject: FIFA World Cup
event_overview.summary: The FIFA World Cup is FIFA’s flagship men’s national-team football tournament. In this context, it refers to the 2026 final competition, staged across Canada, Mexico and the United States, while the selected timeline focuses on post-tournament governance and commercial questions rather than on-field results.

facts.label: Dates
facts.value: The 2026 final competition ran from 11 June to 19 July 2026; the final was scheduled for New York New Jersey Stadium.

facts.label: Hosts and footprint
facts.value: Canada, Mexico and the United States co-hosted the tournament, with matches held across 16 host cities.

facts.label: Governing body
facts.value: FIFA governs the competition. FIFA’s statutes identify the FIFA World Cup as a FIFA competition and provide that its host is decided by the FIFA Congress.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers late-July 2026 debate over FIFA’s reported investment and commercial plans; it does not provide a match-by-match account of the tournament or a full history of the World Cup.
